# X1 closeout: qualification outcome at G0 (offline scientific record)

**Date:** 2026-11-25.

**Owner decision:** accept the final Amendment A1 FAIL (`fb81bef`). X1 G0 confirmatory execution stops. No retry, waiver or further amendment.

**Status:** X1 is closed at preflight. **It produced no confirmatory data.**
- No calibration, main-stage or AWS block ran.
- No X1 hypothesis (H1–H5) was tested.
- Nothing in this document is, or reinterprets, a confirmatory result.

**Descriptive figures:** `reports/x1/X1_CLOSEOUT_DESCRIPTIVE.json`, generated by `scripts/x1_closeout_descriptive.py`.

## 1. Final qualification outcome

**g0m0 (Qwen2.5-7B / RTX 3090 / gpu-node-2, the P0-anchor) is NOT ADMISSIBLE.** Its Phase 1 preflight failed the
sampler on/off equivalence gate under Amendment A1, whose verdict is final (A1.6).

The outcome is **failure to establish equivalence**. It is **not** evidence of an effect exceeding the practical
tolerance.

| Question | Test (A1 data, 24 pairs) | Result | Reading |
|---|---|---|---|
| Is the effect within ±δ? (the pre-registered decision) | TOST, α = 0.05: 90% CI inside (−1.048, +1.048) ms? | CI **[+0.262, +1.445]** ms; upper one-sided p = 0.289 | **Equivalence not established → FAIL** |
| Is the effect larger than +δ? | one-sided t, θ > δ (descriptive) | p = 0.711 | **No evidence** that the effect exceeds the tolerance |
| Is there any effect? | one-sided t, θ > 0 (descriptive, not pre-registered) | p = 0.011; 95% CI [+0.139, +1.567] | A positive ON-condition shift is **detected**, but its size is not resolved relative to δ |

**In words:**
- With the sampler-ON procedure, idle TTFT was slower by an estimated **+0.85 ms** (90% CI +0.26 to +1.44).
- The data cannot exclude a shift as large as +1.44 ms, so the gate fails.
- They also do not show that the shift exceeds 1.05 ms.

The estimand is the effect of the **ON procedure as implemented**: starting the frozen sampler over three ssh calls just
before the segment, then running it at 1 Hz. It is not the sampler's CPU use in isolation. Section 3 explains why this
distinction matters.

## 2. The three Phase 1 attempts and the amendment

| # | Started (UTC) | Rule in force | sampler_equivalence data | Verdict | Commit, record sha256 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 05:16:05 | rev 4 point rule (20 + 20) | on 47.16 vs off 56.50 ms, Δ −9.34 | **FAIL**, plus `sampler_overhead` FAIL (no summary) | `6b6ca7b`, `ef6c6b47…` |
| 2 | 11:43:42 | rev 4 point rule, driver fixed (`80ff3ba`) | on 59.15 vs off 57.92 ms, Δ +1.23 (descriptive bootstrap 95% CI −2.6 to +4.9) | **FAIL** | `9427ddf`, `80f8c46c…` |
| 3 | 12:32:00 | **Amendment A1** (pinned `a5543f2`, manifest `d99bdbae…`) | 3,840 requests, 24 pairs, mean +0.853 ms, 90% CI [+0.262, +1.445], δ 1.048 | **FAIL** | `fb81bef`, `75872fff…` |

All three attempts ran on the same server process: start time 1795583406.76, vLLM 0.17.1, never restarted. Every other
Phase 1 gate passed in attempts 2 and 3: identity, environment, weights, KV capacity, prefix cache, tokenizer parity,
RAM, tokenization, clock offset, and the smoke block (all 14 v5 gates).

**Attempt 1** was invalid as a measurement, for two driver defects (forensics in `ADR-X1-G0M0-P1-RECOVERY`):
- the ON pass re-sent prompts that the OFF pass had just placed in the prefix cache (server log: 0% → 40% hits);
- the sampler was stopped before it could report its own CPU.

**Attempt 2** fixed both defects in the non-frozen driver, under owner approval and with an ADR written before the
re-run. It failed the frozen rule by 0.07 ms.

**Amendment A1** is post hoc and was owner-approved (`x1_amend_a1`). It was drafted after attempts 1 and 2 had failed,
because the rev 4 rule had no defined error rate on this host:
- P(fail | no effect) ≈ 0.53;
- P(pass | a 0.9 ms effect) ≈ 0.45;
- P(pass | a 1.5 ms effect) ≈ 0.36.

It kept the rev 4 tolerance and replaced the decision procedure with a paired-segment TOST:
- 24 balanced OFF/ON pairs × 80 identical-prompt requests;
- a verified cold cache and 3 warm-ups per segment;
- sample size fixed by a simulation whose selection criteria were coded before it first ran.

The proposal, the pin and the single run are each separately approved and committed: `02eafae`, then `0bc1aad` and
`a5543f2`, then `fb81bef`.

The verdicts of attempts 1 and 2 were **never reclassified**, and both records are pinned in the A1 manifest. The
frozen rev 4 rule, reported alongside A1 but not deciding, would have **passed** attempt 3 (+0.58 ms). That shows the
instability A1 was written to remove. It is not a second verdict.

## 3. The observed sampler-associated effect (descriptive)

| Statistic (A1 run) | Value |
|---|---|
| Mean pair difference ON − OFF (pre-registered statistic) | **+0.853 ms** (sd 1.691, SE 0.345, df 23) |
| t-interval 90% / 95% | [+0.262, +1.445] / [+0.139, +1.567] ms |
| Bootstrap 90% / 95% of the mean (20,000 resamples) | [+0.325, +1.428] / [+0.237, +1.551] ms |
| Median pair difference / Hodges–Lehmann | +0.19 / +0.24 ms |
| Pairs with ON slower | 16 of 24 |
| OFF-first pairs / ON-first pairs (order check) | +0.90 / +0.81 ms |

**The effect is intermittent, not a constant shift.**
- **5 of the 24 pairs** (pairs 0, 1, 12, 22 and 23; the ON segments at session positions 1, 2, 25, 45 and 46) show **+3.0 to +5.1 ms**. There, the whole ON segment is slower: p50 55.5–57.6 ms vs 51.8–53.4 ms OFF, with longer upper tails (q90 62–66 vs 54–58 ms).
- **The other 19 pairs** average **+0.04 ms** (sd 0.39).
- **Host telemetry does not separate them.** The 1 Hz host telemetry recorded during ON segments is the same in slow and normal pairs:

  | | slow pairs | other pairs |
  |---|---|---|
  | host CPU (cores) | 1.22 | 1.25 |
  | API server (core) | 0.015 | 0.014 |
  | EngineCore (cores) | 1.19 | 1.22 |

- **The server's own TTFT histogram** shows 33.13 vs 33.14 ms per segment (medians over segments, OFF vs ON). It includes probe and warm-up requests, so it is weak evidence; it suggests the added time lies outside the engine's measured interval.
- **The mechanism is not identified.** One procedural asymmetry exists: only ON segments are preceded by the three ssh sessions that start the sampler. This is noted as a design lesson for X2 and was not investigated further, because that would have meant new measurement.

**Across attempts:**
- Attempt 1's −9.34 ms is a cache artefact, not an estimate of the effect.
- Attempt 2's +1.23 ms (20 + 20) is compatible with attempt 3 but uninformative, with a bootstrap 95% CI of −2.6 to +4.9.
- Only attempt 3 estimates the effect.

**Power.**
- **The noise was worse than the base sizing assumption.** The observed sd(d_k), 1.69 ms, is close to A1's pessimistic sizing scenario (1.79 ms) and above its base scenario (1.16).
- **That did not decide the outcome.** The interval excludes zero, so the result is not an underpowered null; it is a detected shift whose upper bound exceeds δ.
- **The interval's normal approximation is strained.** The five large pairs make the pair differences heavy-tailed. A percentile bootstrap gives a similar interval, but neither changes the pre-registered verdict.

## 4. Why the original 2 × 2 X1 design cannot proceed unchanged

1. **The anchor is inadmissible, permanently.** Rev 4 §9.1: "A fail in either phase makes the platform not admissible: it is reported, never replaced." g0m0 is P0-anchor. Its H1 enters F-X1 with p = 1 and its H2/H3 enter F-X2 with p = 1 (§5).
2. **Every remaining platform's load calibration is anchor-relative.** The approved implementation choice (`docs/X1_FREEZE_CANDIDATE.md` §2, implemented in the frozen `scripts/build_x1.py:grid`) sets each platform's calibration-A grid to `GRID_BASE × s_p`, where s_p is the platform's Phase 1 D-shape decode rate divided by **the G0 anchor's**.
   - The anchor's decode rate was measured (50.89 tok/s), but inside a Phase 1 that failed.
   - The frozen text does not say whether an inadmissible platform's measurement may serve as the reference.
   - Using it, or replacing it, would be a further rule change, which the owner's decision excludes.
   - So the frozen calibration rule cannot be executed for g0m1, g1m0 or g1m1 without a decision X1 is not permitted to make.
3. **The factorial loses its reference cell.**
   - The anchor is the cell shared by the cross-model contrast (g0m0 → g0m1) and the cross-GPU contrast (g0m0 → g1m0).
   - It is also the platform closest to v5 (same model family and serving template).
   - Without it, the 2 × 2 reduces to an unbalanced three-cell design whose contrasts were not pre-registered.
4. **The verdict categories change meaning.**
   - ANCHOR-ONLY becomes impossible.
   - PARTIAL would absorb every outcome short of 3 of 3, mixing "mechanism absent", "host inadmissible" and "low power".
5. **The instrument failed qualification on the G0 host.** P-M (g0m1) runs on the same host with the same sampler procedure. Its qualification is untested, but the evidence makes a pass uncertain. Proceeding there would make X1's G0 column depend on a host where its own telemetry instrument has not been qualified.

## 5. Could the remaining three platforms satisfy the frozen verdict? (in principle only; nothing tested)

**Arithmetic: yes, but only with a clean sweep.** With g0m0 fixed at p = 1:
- **GENERALISES** requires X1-H1 supported on all three of g0m1, g1m0 and g1m1, passing Holm over 4 (thresholds α/4, α/3, α/2 for the three smallest p), **and** H2 equivalent on all three, **and** H4 on all three.
- **ANCHOR-ONLY** is unreachable. Everything else is PARTIAL.

**Approximate probability of 3 of 3 for H1 alone.** This is the cube of the per-platform H1 power in `reports/x1/P0_POWER.md` (n = 24). It assumes independence and ignores the order-dependent Holm thresholds. It was not re-simulated.

| Scenario | per-platform power (normal / empirical) | ≈ P(3 of 3) |
|---|---|---|
| v5 effect 1.565×, v5 noise | 0.929 / 0.974 | **0.80 / 0.92** |
| platform heterogeneity τ = 0.2 | 0.661 / 0.670 | 0.29 / 0.30 |
| 1.5× noise | 0.543 / 0.620 | 0.16 / 0.24 |
| true effect 1.8× | 1.000 / 1.000 | ≈ 1.0 |

**Preconditions the frozen rules cannot satisfy.** Even before power, each remaining platform would need:
- an admissible Phase 1, with A1 qualification on its host;
- a load calibration, which depends on s_p and therefore on the anchor (§4.2).

So the frozen X1 verdict is reachable on paper but not executable as frozen. No claim is made about how g0m1, g1m0 or
g1m1 would behave; none has been tested.

## 6. What X1 does and does not show

**Shows:**
- On the G0 host, Qwen under the vLLM 0.17.1 template passes every identity, environment and capacity check, and the smoke blocks passed all 14 v5 gates in each of the three attempts. Mistral was never started under X1.
- The X1 host sampler's CPU cost is 0.055% of a core.
- The rev 4 point-estimate equivalence rule is unusable at n = 20.
- Under A1, the sampler-ON procedure is associated with an intermittent idle-TTFT slowdown, estimated at +0.85 ms (90% CI +0.26 to +1.44), concentrated in 5 of 24 pairs.

**Does not show:**
- anything about the QuotaShift mechanism on any X1 platform;
- that the sampler effect exceeds 1.05 ms;
- why the slowdown occurs.

**Unchanged:**
- v4/v5 results and every frozen v4/v5/X1 artifact;
- the X1 freeze manifests: Freeze 1 plus A1;
- the three g0m0 records and all raw evidence (git-ignored, with checksums).

**Raw evidence, with checksum files:**
- `reports/x1/g0m0/preflight/attempt1/`
- `reports/x1/g0m0/preflight/attempt2/`
- `reports/x1/g0m0/preflight/evidence_2026-11-25/`
- `reports/x1/g0m0/preflight/A1_RUN_SHA256SUMS`

The local working tree is the only copy of the raw A1 files. They should be added to the backup set under `~/QuotaShift-backups/` with the v5 archives.

**Host state at closeout:**
- gpu-node-2 still serves Qwen under the X1 template, idle, with no sampler running. The rollback command is in `~/x1/ROLLBACK.txt`.
- gpu-node-1 was never touched.
